question: Find the names of the four members of the US women's 3X3 basketball team at the 2020 Olympics. Find out what their final college team was and who the head coach of their final college team was during the 2022/2023 season, as well as the name of the team player with the highest average points per game for that season and the team player with the highest average rebounds per game for that season. Provide a bulleted list with the name of the 3X3 team member, the name of their final college, the name of the coach in the 2022/2023 season, the name of the team player with the highest average points in the 2022/2023 season, and the name of the team player with the highest average rebounds in the 2022/2023 season in a comma separated list for each bullet point. Order the bullet list in alphabetical order by the player's first name. Do not list any other information.
gold_answer:
* Allisha Gray, University of South Carolina, Dawn Staley, Zia Cooke, Aliyah Boston
* Jacquelyn (Jackie) Young, University of Notre Dame, Niele Ivey, Sonia Citron, Olivia Miles
* Kelsey Plum, University of Washington, Tina Langley, Dalayah Daniels, Dalayah Daniels
* Stefanie Dolson, University of Connecticut, Geno Auriemma, Aaliyah Edwards, Dorka Juhasz

The 2020 Summer Olympics women's 3x3 basketball tournament in Tokyo, began on 24 and ended on 28 July 2021. All games were played at the Aomi Urban Sports Park.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_3x3_tournament#cite_note-1)

It was originally scheduled to be held in 2020, but on 24 March 2020, the Olympics were postponed to 2021 due to the COVID-19 pandemic.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_3x3_tournament#cite_note-2) Because of this pandemic, the games were played behind closed doors.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_3x3_tournament#cite_note-3)
The United States won the title after defeating the Russian Olympic team in the final, while China captured the bronze medal over France.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_3x3_tournament#cite_note-4)
The medals for the competition were presented by Samira Asghari, Afghanistan; IOC Member, and the medalists' bouquets were presented by Ingo Weiss, Germany; FIBA Treasurer.
The eight teams played a round robin. The teams placed first and second in the pool qualified for the semifinals. The teams three to six played a playoff. After that, a knockout system was used.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_3x3_tournament#cite_note-5)

# USA Basketball 3x3 at the Olympics
3x3 basketball was featured as an Olympic sport for the first time at the 2020 Tokyo Games (held in 2021). The United States are the only team to medal in multiple Games and made history as the first Olympic 3x3 women’s gold medal winner with a team featuring WNBA players Stefanie Dolson, Allisha Gray, Kelsey Plum and Jackie Young.

# U.S. Women's Team Wins First-Ever 3×3 Gold Medal
## U.S. Women's Team Wins First-Ever 3x3 Gold Medal
Wed, Jul 28, 2021, 2:51 PM
/
USA 3x3 Basketball
Original Article: USA Basketball 3×3
The U.S. Olympic 3×3 Women’s Basketball Team (8-1) earned the first gold medal in Olympic 3×3 basketball history after defeating the Russian Olympic Committee (6-3) 18-15 on Wednesday night at Aomi Urban Sports Park on Saturday in Tokyo.
“It is incredible,” said**Stefanie Dolson**(Chicago Sky/Connecticut/Port Jervis, N.Y.), who led the USA in points and rebounds with seven and nine in the gold medal game. “Basketball runs deep in the USA and to pull this off and win gold is incredible.
China (7-3) beat France (5-5) for the bronze medal.
**Kelsey Plum**(Las Vegas Aces/Washington/Poway, Calif.) added five points,**Allisha Gray**(Dallas Wings/South Carolina/Sandersville, Ga.) notched four points and grabbed six boards and**Jackie Young**(Las Vegas Aces/Notre Dame/Princeton, Ind.) added two points.
“An (Olympic) gold medal, that’s like top tier of my career,” said Gray. “I think the only way to top this is to win another gold medal. I don’t think any other accomplishment of my career can top this. The gold medal sits at the very top.”
Gray put the first point on the board with a free throw 10 seconds into the contest. After ROC tied it up, the USA strung together five-straight points for a 6-1 lead.

# U.S. Women's Team Wins First-Ever 3×3 Gold Medal
## U.S. Women's Team Wins First-Ever 3x3 Gold Medal
The USA and ROC battled back and forth, and with the USA ahead 9-5, the Americans scored a pair of free throws and a 1-pointer to go up 12-5 with 3:53 on the clock. A quick 2-pointer and two more points from ROC cut the USA’s lead to 12-9. ROC was in foul trouble, however, and was whistled for a ninth at 3:07. Young stepped to the line and calmly sunk both her attempts to give her side a 14-9 lead.
ROC came within three points four more times, including the final 18-15 score, but the USA proved too strong and too resilient for the ROC to overcome.
In its semifinal earlier in the evening, the USA held off a tough French (5-4) squad for a 18-16 semifinal win.
Against France, Gray and Plum finished with six points apiece, Dolson scored five and grabbed eight rebounds, while Young added a point.
The U.S. never trailed in the game and was up by four points three times, the last came after Gray scored to make it 12-8 with 4:12 left in the game. France would not back down, however, and rallied back to knot the game at 16-all with 1:07 left on the clock. With 34 ticks remaining, France was whistled for its seventh foul, and Gray scored one of her two tries from the line to push the USA ahead 17-16. Plum scored the USA’s final point from the line with five seconds remaining.
With two seconds left, the ball went out of bounds to France, which called for a timeout. Needing a 2-pointer to send the game into overtime, France’s final shot was off the mark, and the USA advanced to play for gold.
The USA forced six turnovers, won the rebounding battle 18-15 and Gray, Plum and Dolson all recorded a blocked shot.

# U.S. Women's Team Wins First-Ever 3×3 Gold Medal
## U.S. Women's Team Wins First-Ever 3x3 Gold Medal
For the tournament, Plum led all scorers with 6.1 ppg., while Dolson was sixth at 5.7 ppg. and Gray was ninth at 5.3 ppg. Additionally, Gray led all competitors in blocked shots (1.0 bpg.) and tied for the lead in defensive rebounds (3.9 rpg.); Plum and Dolson were No. 1 and No. 2, respectively, in 1-point shooting percentage at 70.0% and 69.0%; while Dolson was third in defensive rebounds at 3.7.
As a team, the USA was No. 1 in six statistical categories, including points per game (19.1), defensive rebounds (12.2 rpg.) and 1-point shooting percentage (62.0%).
The USA coach is**Kara Lawson**(Duke University). In FIBA 3×3 basketball, coaches are not allowed during games.

The 2020 Summer Olympics women's 3x3 basketball tournament in Tokyo, began on 24 and ended on 28 July 2021. All games were played at the Aomi Urban Sports Park.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_3x3_tournament#cite_note-1)
texts.1:
It was originally scheduled to be held in 2020, but on 24 March 2020, the Olympics were postponed to 2021 due to the COVID-19 pandemic.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_3x3_tournament#cite_note-2) Because of this pandemic, the games were played behind closed doors.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_3x3_tournament#cite_note-3)
The United States won the title after defeating the Russian Olympic team in the final, while China captured the bronze medal over France.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_3x3_tournament#cite_note-4)
The medals for the competition were presented by Samira Asghari, Afghanistan; IOC Member, and the medalists' bouquets were presented by Ingo Weiss, Germany; FIBA Treasurer.
The eight teams played a round robin. The teams placed first and second in the pool qualified for the semifinals. The teams three to six played a playoff. After that, a knockout system was used.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_3x3_tournament#cite_note-5)

## U.S. Women's Team Wins First-Ever 3x3 Gold Medal
Wed, Jul 28, 2021, 2:51 PM
/
USA 3x3 Basketball
Original Article: USA Basketball 3×3
The U.S. Olympic 3×3 Women’s Basketball Team (8-1) earned the first gold medal in Olympic 3×3 basketball history after defeating the Russian Olympic Committee (6-3) 18-15 on Wednesday night at Aomi Urban Sports Park on Saturday in Tokyo.
“It is incredible,” said**Stefanie Dolson**(Chicago Sky/Connecticut/Port Jervis, N.Y.), who led the USA in points and rebounds with seven and nine in the gold medal game. “Basketball runs deep in the USA and to pull this off and win gold is incredible.
China (7-3) beat France (5-5) for the bronze medal.
**Kelsey Plum**(Las Vegas Aces/Washington/Poway, Calif.) added five points,**Allisha Gray**(Dallas Wings/South Carolina/Sandersville, Ga.) notched four points and grabbed six boards and**Jackie Young**(Las Vegas Aces/Notre Dame/Princeton, Ind.) added two points.
“An (Olympic) gold medal, that’s like top tier of my career,” said Gray. “I think the only way to top this is to win another gold medal. I don’t think any other accomplishment of my career can top this. The gold medal sits at the very top.”
Gray put the first point on the board with a free throw 10 seconds into the contest. After ROC tied it up, the USA strung together five-straight points for a 6-1 lead.
texts.3:
# U.S. Women's Team Wins First-Ever 3×3 Gold Medal
## U.S. Women's Team Wins First-Ever 3x3 Gold Medal
The USA and ROC battled back and forth, and with the USA ahead 9-5, the Americans scored a pair of free throws and a 1-pointer to go up 12-5 with 3:53 on the clock. A quick 2-pointer and two more points from ROC cut the USA’s lead to 12-9. ROC was in foul trouble, however, and was whistled for a ninth at 3:07. Young stepped to the line and calmly sunk both her attempts to give her side a 14-9 lead.
ROC came within three points four more times, including the final 18-15 score, but the USA proved too strong and too resilient for the ROC to overcome.
In its semifinal earlier in the evening, the USA held off a tough French (5-4) squad for a 18-16 semifinal win.
Against France, Gray and Plum finished with six points apiece, Dolson scored five and grabbed eight rebounds, while Young added a point.
The U.S. never trailed in the game and was up by four points three times, the last came after Gray scored to make it 12-8 with 4:12 left in the game. France would not back down, however, and rallied back to knot the game at 16-all with 1:07 left on the clock. With 34 ticks remaining, France was whistled for its seventh foul, and Gray scored one of her two tries from the line to push the USA ahead 17-16. Plum scored the USA’s final point from the line with five seconds remaining.
With two seconds left, the ball went out of bounds to France, which called for a timeout. Needing a 2-pointer to send the game into overtime, France’s final shot was off the mark, and the USA advanced to play for gold.
The USA forced six turnovers, won the rebounding battle 18-15 and Gray, Plum and Dolson all recorded a blocked shot.

# U.S. Women's Team Wins First-Ever 3×3 Gold Medal
## U.S. Women's Team Wins First-Ever 3x3 Gold Medal
For the tournament, Plum led all scorers with 6.1 ppg., while Dolson was sixth at 5.7 ppg. and Gray was ninth at 5.3 ppg. Additionally, Gray led all competitors in blocked shots (1.0 bpg.) and tied for the lead in defensive rebounds (3.9 rpg.); Plum and Dolson were No. 1 and No. 2, respectively, in 1-point shooting percentage at 70.0% and 69.0%; while Dolson was third in defensive rebounds at 3.7.
As a team, the USA was No. 1 in six statistical categories, including points per game (19.1), defensive rebounds (12.2 rpg.) and 1-point shooting percentage (62.0%).
The USA coach is**Kara Lawson**(Duke University). In FIBA 3×3 basketball, coaches are not allowed during games.

# USA Basketball 3x3 at the Olympics
3x3 basketball was featured as an Olympic sport for the first time at the 2020 Tokyo Games (held in 2021). The United States are the only team to medal in multiple Games and made history as the first Olympic 3x3 women’s gold medal winner with a team featuring WNBA players Stefanie Dolson, Allisha Gray, Kelsey Plum and Jackie Young.

The 2020 Summer Olympics women's 3x3 basketball tournament in Tokyo, began on 24 and ended on 28 July 2021. All games were played at the Aomi Urban Sports Park.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_3x3_tournament#cite_note-1)

It was originally scheduled to be held in 2020, but on 24 March 2020, the Olympics were postponed to 2021 due to the COVID-19 pandemic.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_3x3_tournament#cite_note-2) Because of this pandemic, the games were played behind closed doors.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_3x3_tournament#cite_note-3)
The United States won the title after defeating the Russian Olympic team in the final, while China captured the bronze medal over France.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_3x3_tournament#cite_note-4)
The medals for the competition were presented by Samira Asghari, Afghanistan; IOC Member, and the medalists' bouquets were presented by Ingo Weiss, Germany; FIBA Treasurer.
The eight teams played a round robin. The teams placed first and second in the pool qualified for the semifinals. The teams three to six played a playoff. After that, a knockout system was used.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_3x3_tournament#cite_note-5)

# U.S. Women's Team Wins First-Ever 3×3 Gold Medal
## U.S. Women's Team Wins First-Ever 3x3 Gold Medal
Wed, Jul 28, 2021, 2:51 PM
/
USA 3x3 Basketball
Original Article: USA Basketball 3×3
The U.S. Olympic 3×3 Women’s Basketball Team (8-1) earned the first gold medal in Olympic 3×3 basketball history after defeating the Russian Olympic Committee (6-3) 18-15 on Wednesday night at Aomi Urban Sports Park on Saturday in Tokyo.
“It is incredible,” said**Stefanie Dolson**(Chicago Sky/Connecticut/Port Jervis, N.Y.), who led the USA in points and rebounds with seven and nine in the gold medal game. “Basketball runs deep in the USA and to pull this off and win gold is incredible.
China (7-3) beat France (5-5) for the bronze medal.
**Kelsey Plum**(Las Vegas Aces/Washington/Poway, Calif.) added five points,**Allisha Gray**(Dallas Wings/South Carolina/Sandersville, Ga.) notched four points and grabbed six boards and**Jackie Young**(Las Vegas Aces/Notre Dame/Princeton, Ind.) added two points.
“An (Olympic) gold medal, that’s like top tier of my career,” said Gray. “I think the only way to top this is to win another gold medal. I don’t think any other accomplishment of my career can top this. The gold medal sits at the very top.”
Gray put the first point on the board with a free throw 10 seconds into the contest. After ROC tied it up, the USA strung together five-straight points for a 6-1 lead.

# U.S. Women's Team Wins First-Ever 3×3 Gold Medal
## U.S. Women's Team Wins First-Ever 3x3 Gold Medal
The USA and ROC battled back and forth, and with the USA ahead 9-5, the Americans scored a pair of free throws and a 1-pointer to go up 12-5 with 3:53 on the clock. A quick 2-pointer and two more points from ROC cut the USA’s lead to 12-9. ROC was in foul trouble, however, and was whistled for a ninth at 3:07. Young stepped to the line and calmly sunk both her attempts to give her side a 14-9 lead.
ROC came within three points four more times, including the final 18-15 score, but the USA proved too strong and too resilient for the ROC to overcome.
In its semifinal earlier in the evening, the USA held off a tough French (5-4) squad for a 18-16 semifinal win.
Against France, Gray and Plum finished with six points apiece, Dolson scored five and grabbed eight rebounds, while Young added a point.
The U.S. never trailed in the game and was up by four points three times, the last came after Gray scored to make it 12-8 with 4:12 left in the game. France would not back down, however, and rallied back to knot the game at 16-all with 1:07 left on the clock. With 34 ticks remaining, France was whistled for its seventh foul, and Gray scored one of her two tries from the line to push the USA ahead 17-16. Plum scored the USA’s final point from the line with five seconds remaining.
With two seconds left, the ball went out of bounds to France, which called for a timeout. Needing a 2-pointer to send the game into overtime, France’s final shot was off the mark, and the USA advanced to play for gold.
The USA forced six turnovers, won the rebounding battle 18-15 and Gray, Plum and Dolson all recorded a blocked shot.

# U.S. Women's Team Wins First-Ever 3×3 Gold Medal
## U.S. Women's Team Wins First-Ever 3x3 Gold Medal
For the tournament, Plum led all scorers with 6.1 ppg., while Dolson was sixth at 5.7 ppg. and Gray was ninth at 5.3 ppg. Additionally, Gray led all competitors in blocked shots (1.0 bpg.) and tied for the lead in defensive rebounds (3.9 rpg.); Plum and Dolson were No. 1 and No. 2, respectively, in 1-point shooting percentage at 70.0% and 69.0%; while Dolson was third in defensive rebounds at 3.7.
As a team, the USA was No. 1 in six statistical categories, including points per game (19.1), defensive rebounds (12.2 rpg.) and 1-point shooting percentage (62.0%).
The USA coach is**Kara Lawson**(Duke University). In FIBA 3×3 basketball, coaches are not allowed during games.

## Niele Ivey: Biography at a Glance
*   Niele Ivey, a distinguished former point guard at Notre Dame, made history as the first Black female head coach in Notre Dame history when she assumed the role in 2020.  
*   Under her leadership, Notre Dame has earned an ACC Tournament title and three consecutive Sweet 16 appearances.  
*   As a player at Notre Dame, she earned third-team AP All-America honors and helped secure the 2001 national championship. Ivey also had a five-year WNBA career with the Indiana Fever, Detroit Shock, and Phoenix Mercury.  
*   Before returning to Notre Dame, Ivey was an assistant coach with the Memphis Grizzlies, becoming the ninth active female coach in the NBA.  
*   Ivey’s track record of developing All-American players and NBA stars like her own son Jaden Ivey, and Rookie of the Year Ja Morant, showcases her exceptional mentorship and leadership skills, offering valuable lessons in talent development, teamwork, and performance excellence.  
*   As a former WNBA player and champion, Ivey’s journey from standout athlete to head coach demonstrates her commitment to empowering women and elevating Black voices.

# Niele Ivey
## Biography
Niele Ivey, a distinguished former point guard at Notre Dame, became the fourth Karen & Kevin Keyes Family Head Women’s Basketball Coach on April 22, 2020. As head coach, Ivey has compiled an 89-32 record, securing an ACC Tournament title and leading her team to three consecutive Sweet 16 appearances.
In her fourth season, Ivey guided the Irish to a 28-7 record and an ACC Tournament championship, despite injury challenges. Notre Dame finished the season ranked in the top 25 and achieved notable victories, including wins over No. 8 UConn and No. 5 Virginia Tech.
Ivey’s third season saw Notre Dame win its first regular-season ACC title under her leadership with a 27-6 record. The Irish also made the Sweet 16 and Ivey was named ACC Coach of the Year. She was the only coach nationally to sign three top 20 recruits in 2022 and continues to build a strong future for the program.
In her second season, Ivey orchestrated a major turnaround, leading Notre Dame to a 24-9 record, a Sweet 16 appearance, and a top 20 national ranking.
Before returning to Notre Dame, Ivey spent the 2019-20 season as an assistant coach with the Memphis Grizzlies, becoming the ninth active female coach in the NBA. She played a key role in developing the team’s young players, including NBA Rookie of the Year Ja Morant.
Previously, Ivey served as an assistant coach at Notre Dame from 2007 to 2019, contributing to the program’s decade of dominance, including two national titles and seven Final Fours. Her notable player development includes mentoring All-Americans Skylar Diggins, Jewell Loyd, and Lindsay Allen.
As a player at Notre Dame, she earned third-team AP All-America honors and helped secure the 2001 national championship. Ivey also had a five-year WNBA career with the Indiana Fever, Detroit Shock, and Phoenix Mercury. She graduated from Notre Dame in 2000 with a degree in history.

The **2022–23 Notre Dame Fighting Irish women's basketball team** represented the University of Notre Dame during the [2022–23 NCAA Division I women's basketball season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_NCAA_Division_I_women's_basketball_season "2022–23 NCAA Division I women's basketball season"). The Fighting Irish were led by third-year head coach Niele Ivey, and played their home games at Purcell Pavilion as members of the Atlantic Coast Conference.

The Fighting Irish finished the season 27–6 overall and 15–3 in [ACC play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Atlantic_Coast_Conference_women's_basketball_season "2022–23 Atlantic Coast Conference women's basketball season"), to finish as conference champions. This was their seventh regular season championship, and their first since [2018–19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Notre_Dame_Fighting_Irish_women's_basketball_team "2018–19 Notre Dame Fighting Irish women's basketball team"). As the first seed in the [ACC tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_ACC_women's_basketball_tournament "2023 ACC women's basketball tournament"), they defeated eighth seed [NC State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_NC_State_Wolfpack_women's_basketball_team "2022–23 NC State Wolfpack women's basketball team") in the quarterfinals before losing to fourth seed [Louisville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Louisville_Cardinals_women's_basketball_team "2022–23 Louisville Cardinals women's basketball team") in the semifinals. They received an at-large bid to the [NCAA tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_NCAA_Division_I_women's_basketball_tournament "2023 NCAA Division I women's basketball tournament"), and were the third seed in the [Greenville 1 Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_NCAA_Division_I_women's_basketball_tournament#Greenville_Regional_1_%E2%80%93_Bon_Secours_Wellness_Arena,_Greenville,_SC "2023 NCAA Division I women's basketball tournament").

They defeated fourteenth seed [Southern Utah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Southern_Utah_Thunderbirds_women's_basketball_team "2022–23 Southern Utah Thunderbirds women's basketball team") in the first round and eleventh seed [Mississippi State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Mississippi_State_Bulldogs_women's_basketball_team "2022–23 Mississippi State Bulldogs women's basketball team") in the second round, before losing to second seed [Maryland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Maryland_Terrapins_women's_basketball_team "2022–23 Maryland Terrapins women's basketball team") in the Sweet Sixteen to end their season. Their postseason performance was impacted by an injury to Olivia Miles, who was an All-ACC First Team selection.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Notre_Dame_Fighting_Irish_women's_basketball_team#cite_note-1)

The Fighting Irish finished the season 24–10 overall and 13–5 in [ACC play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_Atlantic_Coast_Conference_women's_basketball_season "2021–22 Atlantic Coast Conference women's basketball season"), to finish in a three-way tie for third place. As the third seed in the [ACC tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_ACC_women's_basketball_tournament "2022 ACC women's basketball tournament"), they defeated sixth seed [Georgia Tech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_Georgia_Tech_Yellow_Jackets_women's_basketball_team "2021–22 Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets women's basketball team") in the quarterfinals before losing to seventh seed [Miami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_Miami_Hurricanes_women's_basketball_team "2021–22 Miami Hurricanes women's basketball team") in the semifinals. They received an at-large bid to the [NCAA tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NCAA_Division_I_women's_basketball_tournament "2022 NCAA Division I women's basketball tournament") and were the fifth seed in the [Bridgeport Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NCAA_Division_I_women's_basketball_tournament#Bridgeport_regional_%E2%80%93_Bridgeport,_Connecticut "2022 NCAA Division I women's basketball tournament").

They defeated twelfth seed UMass in the first round and fourth seed [Oklahoma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_Oklahoma_Sooners_women's_basketball_team "2021–22 Oklahoma Sooners women's basketball team") in the second round, before losing to [NC State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_NC_State_Wolfpack_women's_basketball_team "2021–22 NC State Wolfpack women's basketball team") in the Sweet Sixteen to end their season.

# Niele Ivey
## Niele Ivey: Biography at a Glance
*   Niele Ivey, a distinguished former point guard at Notre Dame, made history as the first Black female head coach in Notre Dame history when she assumed the role in 2020.  
*   Under her leadership, Notre Dame has earned an ACC Tournament title and three consecutive Sweet 16 appearances.  
*   As a player at Notre Dame, she earned third-team AP All-America honors and helped secure the 2001 national championship. Ivey also had a five-year WNBA career with the Indiana Fever, Detroit Shock, and Phoenix Mercury.  
*   Before returning to Notre Dame, Ivey was an assistant coach with the Memphis Grizzlies, becoming the ninth active female coach in the NBA.  
*   Ivey’s track record of developing All-American players and NBA stars like her own son Jaden Ivey, and Rookie of the Year Ja Morant, showcases her exceptional mentorship and leadership skills, offering valuable lessons in talent development, teamwork, and performance excellence.  
*   As a former WNBA player and champion, Ivey’s journey from standout athlete to head coach demonstrates her commitment to empowering women and elevating Black voices.

# Niele Ivey
## Biography
Niele Ivey, a distinguished former point guard at Notre Dame, became the fourth Karen & Kevin Keyes Family Head Women’s Basketball Coach on April 22, 2020. As head coach, Ivey has compiled an 89-32 record, securing an ACC Tournament title and leading her team to three consecutive Sweet 16 appearances.
In her fourth season, Ivey guided the Irish to a 28-7 record and an ACC Tournament championship, despite injury challenges. Notre Dame finished the season ranked in the top 25 and achieved notable victories, including wins over No. 8 UConn and No. 5 Virginia Tech.
Ivey’s third season saw Notre Dame win its first regular-season ACC title under her leadership with a 27-6 record. The Irish also made the Sweet 16 and Ivey was named ACC Coach of the Year. She was the only coach nationally to sign three top 20 recruits in 2022 and continues to build a strong future for the program.
In her second season, Ivey orchestrated a major turnaround, leading Notre Dame to a 24-9 record, a Sweet 16 appearance, and a top 20 national ranking.
Before returning to Notre Dame, Ivey spent the 2019-20 season as an assistant coach with the Memphis Grizzlies, becoming the ninth active female coach in the NBA. She played a key role in developing the team’s young players, including NBA Rookie of the Year Ja Morant.
Previously, Ivey served as an assistant coach at Notre Dame from 2007 to 2019, contributing to the program’s decade of dominance, including two national titles and seven Final Fours. Her notable player development includes mentoring All-Americans Skylar Diggins, Jewell Loyd, and Lindsay Allen.
As a player at Notre Dame, she earned third-team AP All-America honors and helped secure the 2001 national championship. Ivey also had a five-year WNBA career with the Indiana Fever, Detroit Shock, and Phoenix Mercury. She graduated from Notre Dame in 2000 with a degree in history.

texts.5: The **2022–23 Notre Dame Fighting Irish women's basketball team** represented the University of Notre Dame during the [2022–23 NCAA Division I women's basketball season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_NCAA_Division_I_women's_basketball_season "2022–23 NCAA Division I women's basketball season"). The Fighting Irish were led by third-year head coach Niele Ivey, and played their home games at Purcell Pavilion as members of the Atlantic Coast Conference.
texts.6: The Fighting Irish finished the season 27–6 overall and 15–3 in [ACC play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Atlantic_Coast_Conference_women's_basketball_season "2022–23 Atlantic Coast Conference women's basketball season"), to finish as conference champions. This was their seventh regular season championship, and their first since [2018–19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Notre_Dame_Fighting_Irish_women's_basketball_team "2018–19 Notre Dame Fighting Irish women's basketball team"). As the first seed in the [ACC tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_ACC_women's_basketball_tournament "2023 ACC women's basketball tournament"), they defeated eighth seed [NC State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_NC_State_Wolfpack_women's_basketball_team "2022–23 NC State Wolfpack women's basketball team") in the quarterfinals before losing to fourth seed [Louisville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Louisville_Cardinals_women's_basketball_team "2022–23 Louisville Cardinals women's basketball team") in the semifinals. They received an at-large bid to the [NCAA tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_NCAA_Division_I_women's_basketball_tournament "2023 NCAA Division I women's basketball tournament"), and were the third seed in the [Greenville 1 Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_NCAA_Division_I_women's_basketball_tournament#Greenville_Regional_1_%E2%80%93_Bon_Secours_Wellness_Arena,_Greenville,_SC "2023 NCAA Division I women's basketball tournament").
texts.7: They defeated fourteenth seed [Southern Utah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Southern_Utah_Thunderbirds_women's_basketball_team "2022–23 Southern Utah Thunderbirds women's basketball team") in the first round and eleventh seed [Mississippi State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Mississippi_State_Bulldogs_women's_basketball_team "2022–23 Mississippi State Bulldogs women's basketball team") in the second round, before losing to second seed [Maryland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Maryland_Terrapins_women's_basketball_team "2022–23 Maryland Terrapins women's basketball team") in the Sweet Sixteen to end their season. Their postseason performance was impacted by an injury to Olivia Miles, who was an All-ACC First Team selection.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Notre_Dame_Fighting_Irish_women's_basketball_team#cite_note-1)
texts.8: The Fighting Irish finished the season 24–10 overall and 13–5 in [ACC play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_Atlantic_Coast_Conference_women's_basketball_season "2021–22 Atlantic Coast Conference women's basketball season"), to finish in a three-way tie for third place. As the third seed in the [ACC tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_ACC_women's_basketball_tournament "2022 ACC women's basketball tournament"), they defeated sixth seed [Georgia Tech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_Georgia_Tech_Yellow_Jackets_women's_basketball_team "2021–22 Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets women's basketball team") in the quarterfinals before losing to seventh seed [Miami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_Miami_Hurricanes_women's_basketball_team "2021–22 Miami Hurricanes women's basketball team") in the semifinals. They received an at-large bid to the [NCAA tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NCAA_Division_I_women's_basketball_tournament "2022 NCAA Division I women's basketball tournament") and were the fifth seed in the [Bridgeport Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NCAA_Division_I_women's_basketball_tournament#Bridgeport_regional_%E2%80%93_Bridgeport,_Connecticut "2022 NCAA Division I women's basketball tournament").

## Niele Ivey: Biography at a Glance
*   Niele Ivey, a distinguished former point guard at Notre Dame, made history as the first Black female head coach in Notre Dame history when she assumed the role in 2020.  
*   Under her leadership, Notre Dame has earned an ACC Tournament title and three consecutive Sweet 16 appearances.  
*   As a player at Notre Dame, she earned third-team AP All-America honors and helped secure the 2001 national championship. Ivey also had a five-year WNBA career with the Indiana Fever, Detroit Shock, and Phoenix Mercury.  
*   Before returning to Notre Dame, Ivey was an assistant coach with the Memphis Grizzlies, becoming the ninth active female coach in the NBA.  
*   Ivey’s track record of developing All-American players and NBA stars like her own son Jaden Ivey, and Rookie of the Year Ja Morant, showcases her exceptional mentorship and leadership skills, offering valuable lessons in talent development, teamwork, and performance excellence.  
*   As a former WNBA player and champion, Ivey’s journey from standout athlete to head coach demonstrates her commitment to empowering women and elevating Black voices.

# Niele Ivey
## Biography
Niele Ivey, a distinguished former point guard at Notre Dame, became the fourth Karen & Kevin Keyes Family Head Women’s Basketball Coach on April 22, 2020. As head coach, Ivey has compiled an 89-32 record, securing an ACC Tournament title and leading her team to three consecutive Sweet 16 appearances.
In her fourth season, Ivey guided the Irish to a 28-7 record and an ACC Tournament championship, despite injury challenges. Notre Dame finished the season ranked in the top 25 and achieved notable victories, including wins over No. 8 UConn and No. 5 Virginia Tech.
Ivey’s third season saw Notre Dame win its first regular-season ACC title under her leadership with a 27-6 record. The Irish also made the Sweet 16 and Ivey was named ACC Coach of the Year. She was the only coach nationally to sign three top 20 recruits in 2022 and continues to build a strong future for the program.
In her second season, Ivey orchestrated a major turnaround, leading Notre Dame to a 24-9 record, a Sweet 16 appearance, and a top 20 national ranking.
Before returning to Notre Dame, Ivey spent the 2019-20 season as an assistant coach with the Memphis Grizzlies, becoming the ninth active female coach in the NBA. She played a key role in developing the team’s young players, including NBA Rookie of the Year Ja Morant.
Previously, Ivey served as an assistant coach at Notre Dame from 2007 to 2019, contributing to the program’s decade of dominance, including two national titles and seven Final Fours. Her notable player development includes mentoring All-Americans Skylar Diggins, Jewell Loyd, and Lindsay Allen.
As a player at Notre Dame, she earned third-team AP All-America honors and helped secure the 2001 national championship. Ivey also had a five-year WNBA career with the Indiana Fever, Detroit Shock, and Phoenix Mercury. She graduated from Notre Dame in 2000 with a degree in history.

The **2022–23 Notre Dame Fighting Irish women's basketball team** represented the University of Notre Dame during the [2022–23 NCAA Division I women's basketball season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_NCAA_Division_I_women's_basketball_season "2022–23 NCAA Division I women's basketball season"). The Fighting Irish were led by third-year head coach Niele Ivey, and played their home games at Purcell Pavilion as members of the Atlantic Coast Conference.

The Fighting Irish finished the season 27–6 overall and 15–3 in [ACC play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Atlantic_Coast_Conference_women's_basketball_season "2022–23 Atlantic Coast Conference women's basketball season"), to finish as conference champions. This was their seventh regular season championship, and their first since [2018–19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Notre_Dame_Fighting_Irish_women's_basketball_team "2018–19 Notre Dame Fighting Irish women's basketball team"). As the first seed in the [ACC tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_ACC_women's_basketball_tournament "2023 ACC women's basketball tournament"), they defeated eighth seed [NC State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_NC_State_Wolfpack_women's_basketball_team "2022–23 NC State Wolfpack women's basketball team") in the quarterfinals before losing to fourth seed [Louisville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Louisville_Cardinals_women's_basketball_team "2022–23 Louisville Cardinals women's basketball team") in the semifinals. They received an at-large bid to the [NCAA tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_NCAA_Division_I_women's_basketball_tournament "2023 NCAA Division I women's basketball tournament"), and were the third seed in the [Greenville 1 Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_NCAA_Division_I_women's_basketball_tournament#Greenville_Regional_1_%E2%80%93_Bon_Secours_Wellness_Arena,_Greenville,_SC "2023 NCAA Division I women's basketball tournament").

They defeated fourteenth seed [Southern Utah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Southern_Utah_Thunderbirds_women's_basketball_team "2022–23 Southern Utah Thunderbirds women's basketball team") in the first round and eleventh seed [Mississippi State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Mississippi_State_Bulldogs_women's_basketball_team "2022–23 Mississippi State Bulldogs women's basketball team") in the second round, before losing to second seed [Maryland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Maryland_Terrapins_women's_basketball_team "2022–23 Maryland Terrapins women's basketball team") in the Sweet Sixteen to end their season. Their postseason performance was impacted by an injury to Olivia Miles, who was an All-ACC First Team selection.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Notre_Dame_Fighting_Irish_women's_basketball_team#cite_note-1)

The Fighting Irish finished the season 24–10 overall and 13–5 in [ACC play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_Atlantic_Coast_Conference_women's_basketball_season "2021–22 Atlantic Coast Conference women's basketball season"), to finish in a three-way tie for third place. As the third seed in the [ACC tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_ACC_women's_basketball_tournament "2022 ACC women's basketball tournament"), they defeated sixth seed [Georgia Tech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_Georgia_Tech_Yellow_Jackets_women's_basketball_team "2021–22 Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets women's basketball team") in the quarterfinals before losing to seventh seed [Miami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_Miami_Hurricanes_women's_basketball_team "2021–22 Miami Hurricanes women's basketball team") in the semifinals. They received an at-large bid to the [NCAA tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NCAA_Division_I_women's_basketball_tournament "2022 NCAA Division I women's basketball tournament") and were the fifth seed in the [Bridgeport Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NCAA_Division_I_women's_basketball_tournament#Bridgeport_regional_%E2%80%93_Bridgeport,_Connecticut "2022 NCAA Division I women's basketball tournament").

They defeated twelfth seed UMass in the first round and fourth seed [Oklahoma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_Oklahoma_Sooners_women's_basketball_team "2021–22 Oklahoma Sooners women's basketball team") in the second round, before losing to [NC State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_NC_State_Wolfpack_women's_basketball_team "2021–22 NC State Wolfpack women's basketball team") in the Sweet Sixteen to end their season.

The **2022–23 UConn Huskies women's basketball team** represented the University of Connecticut (UConn) during the [2022–23 NCAA Division I women's basketball season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_NCAA_Division_I_women's_basketball_season "2022–23 NCAA Division I women's basketball season"). The Huskies, led by Hall of Fame head coach Geno Auriemma in his 38th season at UConn, split their home games between Harry A. Gampel Pavilion on their campus in Storrs and the XL Center in Hartford, Connecticut. UConn is a member of the Big East Conference, which it joined in the 2020–21 season; it had been a member of the original Big East Conference from 1979 through 2013, and one of the original women's basketball teams in that conference in 1982.[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UConn_Huskies_women's_basketball_team#cite_note-1)

The Huskies finished an injury-plagued previous season with a record of 30–6, losing the [championship game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NCAA_Division_I_women's_basketball_championship_game "2022 NCAA Division I women's basketball championship game") of the [2022 NCAA women's basketball tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NCAA_Division_I_women's_basketball_tournament "2022 NCAA Division I women's basketball tournament") to South Carolina. Three graduates from that squad were selected in the 2022 WNBA draft, but with six returning starters including the backcourt of Paige Bueckers, Azzi Fudd, and Nika Mühl, with forwards Dorka Juhász, Aaliyah Edwards, and Caroline Ducharme, UConn was expected to win the much improved Big East again. Bueckers tore an ACL in a pickup game before fall workouts,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UConn_Huskies_women's_basketball_team#cite_note-2) and five-star recruit Ice Brady suffered a tendon dislocation during an early practice; both players underwent season ending surgeries and sat on the bench all season.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UConn_Huskies_women's_basketball_team#cite_note-3)

Starting the season already down two players, UConn played surprisingly well against early opponents, with strong wins against #3 Texas, #10 NC State, and #9 Iowa in the first weeks. In the Texas game, Juhász injured a thumb and was sidelined for several weeks. Aubrey Griffin, who had redshirted the previous season because of injury, and Lou Lopez Sénéchal, a graduate transfer shooting guard from Fairfield University, got some starts and immediately impacted the team with their durability and shooting proficiency. Fudd began the season as a leading scorer, with Mühl leading the country in assists per game, and Edwards seemingly unstoppable in the paint. Fudd was injured in the loss to #7 Notre Dame, and by the end of December the Huskies only had seven players healthy, even after Juhász's return. On January 8, UConn's contest against DePaul was postponed because the Huskies only had six players able to play.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UConn_Huskies_women's_basketball_team#cite_note-4)

Even with a short bench, the Huskies continued to win January, dominating most conference opponents and picking up another quality win at Tennessee, the only team to score more than 60 points against the fierce UConn team defense in January. In early February the team matched up against the #1 ranked South Carolina Gamecocks with a sold-out home crowd in the XL Center but lost 81–77. Three days later, Marquette upset the noticeably worn-out Huskies in a tight defensive battle, UConn's first consecutive loss in 30 years. While UConn was able to twice defeat rival Villanova, several Big East teams strongly tested the still-shorthanded and battered Huskies, St. John's outscoring them by five. UConn finished their regular season with an overall record of 26–5 and a conference record of 18–2. They won the Big East regular season championship and were the top seed in the [conference tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Big_East_women's_basketball_tournament "2023 Big East women's basketball tournament"). Azzi Fudd and Caroline Ducharme, who both missed a significant part of the regular season due to injury, returned in time for the Big East tournament, and with the UConn squad healthy for the first time since its first games, the Huskies methodically notched three consecutive wins to emerge as tournament champions, getting the automatic bid to the [2023 NCAA women's basketball tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_NCAA_Division_I_women's_basketball_tournament "2023 NCAA Division I women's basketball tournament"). In the NCAA tournament, UConn advanced to their 29th consecutive Sweet Sixteen with wins over Vermont and Baylor. However, they lost to Ohio St. in the next round, ending their Final Four streak at 14. The Huskies finished their season with a 31–6 record.

With most of their roster either injured or in-development during the season, the Huskies relied heavily on several players for the first time. Mühl, the team's new point guard, set a UConn single-season record with 284 assists. Edwards was the team's leading scorer and a third team All-American. Lopez Sénéchal and Juhász, who had both transferred from other schools in the previous two years, put up solid numbers, as did Griffin, who had missed the previous season.
UConn was ranked no. 2 in both the 2021 AP and Coaches pre-season polls. After some early struggles, they finished the regular season with a record of 22–5, including 16–1 in the Big East to win the conference regular season championship. UConn then won the [Big East tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Big_East_women's_basketball_tournament "2022 Big East women's basketball tournament"). As a no. 2 seed in the NCAA tournament, they advanced to the championship game, where they lost to South Carolina. UConn finished their campaign with a record of 30–6.
The Huskies graduated senior starters Christyn Williams, Olivia Nelson-Ododa, and Evina Westbrook from the 2021–22 roster, each of them being drafted into the [Women's National Basketball Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women's_National_Basketball_Association "Women's National Basketball Association"). Sophomore Piath Gabriel chose to enter the transfer portal during the offseason and accepted a scholarship at UMass.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UConn_Huskies_women's_basketball_team#cite_note-07072022UMassGabrieltransfer-5)

The **2022–23 UConn Huskies women's basketball team** represented the University of Connecticut (UConn) during the [2022–23 NCAA Division I women's basketball season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_NCAA_Division_I_women's_basketball_season "2022–23 NCAA Division I women's basketball season"). The Huskies, led by Hall of Fame head coach Geno Auriemma in his 38th season at UConn, split their home games between Harry A. Gampel Pavilion on their campus in Storrs and the XL Center in Hartford, Connecticut. UConn is a member of the Big East Conference, which it joined in the 2020–21 season; it had been a member of the original Big East Conference from 1979 through 2013, and one of the original women's basketball teams in that conference in 1982.[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UConn_Huskies_women's_basketball_team#cite_note-1)
texts.5: The Huskies finished an injury-plagued previous season with a record of 30–6, losing the [championship game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NCAA_Division_I_women's_basketball_championship_game "2022 NCAA Division I women's basketball championship game") of the [2022 NCAA women's basketball tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NCAA_Division_I_women's_basketball_tournament "2022 NCAA Division I women's basketball tournament") to South Carolina. Three graduates from that squad were selected in the 2022 WNBA draft, but with six returning starters including the backcourt of Paige Bueckers, Azzi Fudd, and Nika Mühl, with forwards Dorka Juhász, Aaliyah Edwards, and Caroline Ducharme, UConn was expected to win the much improved Big East again. Bueckers tore an ACL in a pickup game before fall workouts,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UConn_Huskies_women's_basketball_team#cite_note-2) and five-star recruit Ice Brady suffered a tendon dislocation during an early practice; both players underwent season ending surgeries and sat on the bench all season.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UConn_Huskies_women's_basketball_team#cite_note-3)
texts.6: Starting the season already down two players, UConn played surprisingly well against early opponents, with strong wins against #3 Texas, #10 NC State, and #9 Iowa in the first weeks. In the Texas game, Juhász injured a thumb and was sidelined for several weeks. Aubrey Griffin, who had redshirted the previous season because of injury, and Lou Lopez Sénéchal, a graduate transfer shooting guard from Fairfield University, got some starts and immediately impacted the team with their durability and shooting proficiency. Fudd began the season as a leading scorer, with Mühl leading the country in assists per game, and Edwards seemingly unstoppable in the paint. Fudd was injured in the loss to #7 Notre Dame, and by the end of December the Huskies only had seven players healthy, even after Juhász's return. On January 8, UConn's contest against DePaul was postponed because the Huskies only had six players able to play.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UConn_Huskies_women's_basketball_team#cite_note-4)
texts.7: Even with a short bench, the Huskies continued to win January, dominating most conference opponents and picking up another quality win at Tennessee, the only team to score more than 60 points against the fierce UConn team defense in January. In early February the team matched up against the #1 ranked South Carolina Gamecocks with a sold-out home crowd in the XL Center but lost 81–77. Three days later, Marquette upset the noticeably worn-out Huskies in a tight defensive battle, UConn's first consecutive loss in 30 years. While UConn was able to twice defeat rival Villanova, several Big East teams strongly tested the still-shorthanded and battered Huskies, St. John's outscoring them by five. UConn finished their regular season with an overall record of 26–5 and a conference record of 18–2. They won the Big East regular season championship and were the top seed in the [conference tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Big_East_women's_basketball_tournament "2023 Big East women's basketball tournament"). Azzi Fudd and Caroline Ducharme, who both missed a significant part of the regular season due to injury, returned in time for the Big East tournament, and with the UConn squad healthy for the first time since its first games, the Huskies methodically notched three consecutive wins to emerge as tournament champions, getting the automatic bid to the [2023 NCAA women's basketball tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_NCAA_Division_I_women's_basketball_tournament "2023 NCAA Division I women's basketball tournament"). In the NCAA tournament, UConn advanced to their 29th consecutive Sweet Sixteen with wins over Vermont and Baylor. However, they lost to Ohio St. in the next round, ending their Final Four streak at 14. The Huskies finished their season with a 31–6 record.
texts.8:
With most of their roster either injured or in-development during the season, the Huskies relied heavily on several players for the first time. Mühl, the team's new point guard, set a UConn single-season record with 284 assists. Edwards was the team's leading scorer and a third team All-American. Lopez Sénéchal and Juhász, who had both transferred from other schools in the previous two years, put up solid numbers, as did Griffin, who had missed the previous season.
UConn was ranked no. 2 in both the 2021 AP and Coaches pre-season polls. After some early struggles, they finished the regular season with a record of 22–5, including 16–1 in the Big East to win the conference regular season championship. UConn then won the [Big East tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Big_East_women's_basketball_tournament "2022 Big East women's basketball tournament"). As a no. 2 seed in the NCAA tournament, they advanced to the championship game, where they lost to South Carolina. UConn finished their campaign with a record of 30–6.
The Huskies graduated senior starters Christyn Williams, Olivia Nelson-Ododa, and Evina Westbrook from the 2021–22 roster, each of them being drafted into the [Women's National Basketball Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women's_National_Basketball_Association "Women's National Basketball Association"). Sophomore Piath Gabriel chose to enter the transfer portal during the offseason and accepted a scholarship at UMass.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UConn_Huskies_women's_basketball_team#cite_note-07072022UMassGabrieltransfer-5)

#### Recruiting class of 2024
Hall of Fame head coach Geno Auriemma and Hall of Fame associate head coach Chris Dailey returned for their 38th season. Assistant coach Jamelle Elliott was a UConn assistant coach from 1998 to 2009 and returned after a nine-year head coaching stint at [Cincinnati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cincinnati_Bearcats_women's_basketball "Cincinnati Bearcats women's basketball"). Assistant coach Morgan Valley was the head coach of the [Hartford Hawks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hartford_Hawks_women's_basketball "Hartford Hawks women's basketball") when hired by the Huskies. The **2022–23 UConn Huskies women's basketball team** represented the University of Connecticut (UConn) during the [2022–23 NCAA Division I women's basketball season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_NCAA_Division_I_women's_basketball_season "2022–23 NCAA Division I women's basketball season"). The Huskies, led by Hall of Fame head coach Geno Auriemma in his 38th season at UConn, split their home games between Harry A. Gampel Pavilion on their campus in Storrs and the XL Center in Hartford, Connecticut. UConn is a member of the Big East Conference, which it joined in the 2020–21 season; it had been a member of the original Big East Conference from 1979 through 2013, and one of the original women's basketball teams in that conference in 1982.[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UConn_Huskies_women's_basketball_team#cite_note-1)

The Huskies finished an injury-plagued previous season with a record of 30–6, losing the [championship game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NCAA_Division_I_women's_basketball_championship_game "2022 NCAA Division I women's basketball championship game") of the [2022 NCAA women's basketball tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NCAA_Division_I_women's_basketball_tournament "2022 NCAA Division I women's basketball tournament") to South Carolina. Three graduates from that squad were selected in the 2022 WNBA draft, but with six returning starters including the backcourt of Paige Bueckers, Azzi Fudd, and Nika Mühl, with forwards Dorka Juhász, Aaliyah Edwards, and Caroline Ducharme, UConn was expected to win the much improved Big East again. Bueckers tore an ACL in a pickup game before fall workouts,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UConn_Huskies_women's_basketball_team#cite_note-2) and five-star recruit Ice Brady suffered a tendon dislocation during an early practice; both players underwent season ending surgeries and sat on the bench all season.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UConn_Huskies_women's_basketball_team#cite_note-3)

Starting the season already down two players, UConn played surprisingly well against early opponents, with strong wins against #3 Texas, #10 NC State, and #9 Iowa in the first weeks. In the Texas game, Juhász injured a thumb and was sidelined for several weeks. Aubrey Griffin, who had redshirted the previous season because of injury, and Lou Lopez Sénéchal, a graduate transfer shooting guard from Fairfield University, got some starts and immediately impacted the team with their durability and shooting proficiency. Fudd began the season as a leading scorer, with Mühl leading the country in assists per game, and Edwards seemingly unstoppable in the paint. Fudd was injured in the loss to #7 Notre Dame, and by the end of December the Huskies only had seven players healthy, even after Juhász's return. On January 8, UConn's contest against DePaul was postponed because the Huskies only had six players able to play.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UConn_Huskies_women's_basketball_team#cite_note-4)

Even with a short bench, the Huskies continued to win January, dominating most conference opponents and picking up another quality win at Tennessee, the only team to score more than 60 points against the fierce UConn team defense in January. In early February the team matched up against the #1 ranked South Carolina Gamecocks with a sold-out home crowd in the XL Center but lost 81–77. Three days later, Marquette upset the noticeably worn-out Huskies in a tight defensive battle, UConn's first consecutive loss in 30 years. While UConn was able to twice defeat rival Villanova, several Big East teams strongly tested the still-shorthanded and battered Huskies, St. John's outscoring them by five. UConn finished their regular season with an overall record of 26–5 and a conference record of 18–2. They won the Big East regular season championship and were the top seed in the [conference tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Big_East_women's_basketball_tournament "2023 Big East women's basketball tournament"). Azzi Fudd and Caroline Ducharme, who both missed a significant part of the regular season due to injury, returned in time for the Big East tournament, and with the UConn squad healthy for the first time since its first games, the Huskies methodically notched three consecutive wins to emerge as tournament champions, getting the automatic bid to the [2023 NCAA women's basketball tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_NCAA_Division_I_women's_basketball_tournament "2023 NCAA Division I women's basketball tournament"). In the NCAA tournament, UConn advanced to their 29th consecutive Sweet Sixteen with wins over Vermont and Baylor. However, they lost to Ohio St. in the next round, ending their Final Four streak at 14. The Huskies finished their season with a 31–6 record.

With most of their roster either injured or in-development during the season, the Huskies relied heavily on several players for the first time. Mühl, the team's new point guard, set a UConn single-season record with 284 assists. Edwards was the team's leading scorer and a third team All-American. Lopez Sénéchal and Juhász, who had both transferred from other schools in the previous two years, put up solid numbers, as did Griffin, who had missed the previous season.
UConn was ranked no. 2 in both the 2021 AP and Coaches pre-season polls. After some early struggles, they finished the regular season with a record of 22–5, including 16–1 in the Big East to win the conference regular season championship. UConn then won the [Big East tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Big_East_women's_basketball_tournament "2022 Big East women's basketball tournament"). As a no. 2 seed in the NCAA tournament, they advanced to the championship game, where they lost to South Carolina. UConn finished their campaign with a record of 30–6.
The Huskies graduated senior starters Christyn Williams, Olivia Nelson-Ododa, and Evina Westbrook from the 2021–22 roster, each of them being drafted into the [Women's National Basketball Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women's_National_Basketball_Association "Women's National Basketball Association"). Sophomore Piath Gabriel chose to enter the transfer portal during the offseason and accepted a scholarship at UMass.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UConn_Huskies_women's_basketball_team#cite_note-07072022UMassGabrieltransfer-5)

Bueckers tore an ACL in a pickup game before fall workouts,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UConn_Huskies_women's_basketball_team#cite_note-2) and five-star recruit Ice Brady suffered a tendon dislocation during an early practice; both players underwent season ending surgeries and sat on the bench all season.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UConn_Huskies_women's_basketball_team#cite_note-3)

Starting the season already down two players, UConn played surprisingly well against early opponents, with strong wins against #3 Texas, #10 NC State, and #9 Iowa in the first weeks. In the Texas game, Juhász injured a thumb and was sidelined for several weeks. Aubrey Griffin, who had redshirted the previous season because of injury, and Lou Lopez Sénéchal, a graduate transfer shooting guard from Fairfield University, got some starts and immediately impacted the team with their durability and shooting proficiency. Fudd began the season as a leading scorer, with Mühl leading the country in assists per game, and Edwards seemingly unstoppable in the paint. Fudd was injured in the loss to #7 Notre Dame, and by the end of December the Huskies only had seven players healthy, even after Juhász's return. On January 8, UConn's contest against DePaul was postponed because the Huskies only had six players able to play.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UConn_Huskies_women's_basketball_team#cite_note-4)

Even with a short bench, the Huskies continued to win January, dominating most conference opponents and picking up another quality win at Tennessee, the only team to score more than 60 points against the fierce UConn team defense in January. In early February the team matched up against the #1 ranked South Carolina Gamecocks with a sold-out home crowd in the XL Center but lost 81–77. Three days later, Marquette upset the noticeably worn-out Huskies in a tight defensive battle, UConn's first consecutive loss in 30 years. While UConn was able to twice defeat rival Villanova, several Big East teams strongly tested the still-shorthanded and battered Huskies, St. John's outscoring them by five. UConn finished their regular season with an overall record of 26–5 and a conference record of 18–2. They won the Big East regular season championship and were the top seed in the [conference tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Big_East_women's_basketball_tournament "2023 Big East women's basketball tournament"). Azzi Fudd and Caroline Ducharme, who both missed a significant part of the regular season due to injury, returned in time for the Big East tournament, and with the UConn squad healthy for the first time since its first games, the Huskies methodically notched three consecutive wins to emerge as tournament champions, getting the automatic bid to the [2023 NCAA women's basketball tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_NCAA_Division_I_women's_basketball_tournament "2023 NCAA Division I women's basketball tournament"). In the NCAA tournament, UConn advanced to their 29th consecutive Sweet Sixteen with wins over Vermont and Baylor. However, they lost to Ohio St. in the next round, ending their Final Four streak at 14. The Huskies finished their season with a 31–6 record.

With most of their roster either injured or in-development during the season, the Huskies relied heavily on several players for the first time. Mühl, the team's new point guard, set a UConn single-season record with 284 assists. Edwards was the team's leading scorer and a third team All-American. Lopez Sénéchal and Juhász, who had both transferred from other schools in the previous two years, put up solid numbers, as did Griffin, who had missed the previous season.
UConn was ranked no. 2 in both the 2021 AP and Coaches pre-season polls. After some early struggles, they finished the regular season with a record of 22–5, including 16–1 in the Big East to win the conference regular season championship. UConn then won the [Big East tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Big_East_women's_basketball_tournament "2022 Big East women's basketball tournament"). As a no. 2 seed in the NCAA tournament, they advanced to the championship game, where they lost to South Carolina. UConn finished their campaign with a record of 30–6.
The Huskies graduated senior starters Christyn Williams, Olivia Nelson-Ododa, and Evina Westbrook from the 2021–22 roster, each of them being drafted into the [Women's National Basketball Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women's_National_Basketball_Association "Women's National Basketball Association"). Sophomore Piath Gabriel chose to enter the transfer portal during the offseason and accepted a scholarship at UMass.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UConn_Huskies_women's_basketball_team#cite_note-07072022UMassGabrieltransfer-5)

UConn lost two players to knee injuries during the 2022 offseason. On August 1, superstar guard Paige Bueckerstore her left ACL during a pick-up game, and UConn announced two days later that she would miss the entire 2022–23 season.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UConn_Huskies_women's_basketball_team#cite_note-7) Then, during a Huskies practice on October 21, freshman forward Ice Brady dislocated her right patellar tendon; she underwent season-ending surgery on October 25.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UConn_Huskies_women's_basketball_team#cite_note-8)
The Huskies had another excellent recruiting class. ESPN ranked Patterson as the fourth-best recruit of the 2022 class and Brady as the fifth-best. Brady would be lost for the 2022–23 season to a knee injury. Bettencourt was recruited just before the start of the season.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UConn_Huskies_women's_basketball_team#cite_note-9)

Harry A. Gampel Pavilion, where the Huskies played home games
The **2022–23 UConn Huskies women's basketball team** represented the University of Connecticut (UConn) during the [2022–23 NCAA Division I women's basketball season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_NCAA_Division_I_women's_basketball_season "2022–23 NCAA Division I women's basketball season"). The Huskies, led by Hall of Fame head coach Geno Auriemma in his 38th season at UConn, split their home games between Harry A. Gampel Pavilion on their campus in Storrs and the XL Center in Hartford, Connecticut. UConn is a member of the Big East Conference, which it joined in the 2020–21 season; it had been a member of the original Big East Conference from 1979 through 2013, and one of the original women's basketball teams in that conference in 1982.[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UConn_Huskies_women's_basketball_team#cite_note-1)
texts.5: The Huskies finished an injury-plagued previous season with a record of 30–6, losing the [championship game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NCAA_Division_I_women's_basketball_championship_game "2022 NCAA Division I women's basketball championship game") of the [2022 NCAA women's basketball tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NCAA_Division_I_women's_basketball_tournament "2022 NCAA Division I women's basketball tournament") to South Carolina. Three graduates from that squad were selected in the 2022 WNBA draft, but with six returning starters including the backcourt of Paige Bueckers, Azzi Fudd, and Nika Mühl, with forwards Dorka Juhász, Aaliyah Edwards, and Caroline Ducharme, UConn was expected to win the much improved Big East again. Bueckers tore an ACL in a pickup game before fall workouts,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UConn_Huskies_women's_basketball_team#cite_note-2) and five-star recruit Ice Brady suffered a tendon dislocation during an early practice; both players underwent season ending surgeries and sat on the bench all season.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UConn_Huskies_women's_basketball_team#cite_note-3)
texts.6: Starting the season already down two players, UConn played surprisingly well against early opponents, with strong wins against #3 Texas, #10 NC State, and #9 Iowa in the first weeks. In the Texas game, Juhász injured a thumb and was sidelined for several weeks. Aubrey Griffin, who had redshirted the previous season because of injury, and Lou Lopez Sénéchal, a graduate transfer shooting guard from Fairfield University, got some starts and immediately impacted the team with their durability and shooting proficiency. Fudd began the season as a leading scorer, with Mühl leading the country in assists per game, and Edwards seemingly unstoppable in the paint. Fudd was injured in the loss to #7 Notre Dame, and by the end of December the Huskies only had seven players healthy, even after Juhász's return. On January 8, UConn's contest against DePaul was postponed because the Huskies only had six players able to play.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UConn_Huskies_women's_basketball_team#cite_note-4)
texts.7: Even with a short bench, the Huskies continued to win January, dominating most conference opponents and picking up another quality win at Tennessee, the only team to score more than 60 points against the fierce UConn team defense in January. In early February the team matched up against the #1 ranked South Carolina Gamecocks with a sold-out home crowd in the XL Center but lost 81–77. Three days later, Marquette upset the noticeably worn-out Huskies in a tight defensive battle, UConn's first consecutive loss in 30 years. While UConn was able to twice defeat rival Villanova, several Big East teams strongly tested the still-shorthanded and battered Huskies, St. John's outscoring them by five. UConn finished their regular season with an overall record of 26–5 and a conference record of 18–2. They won the Big East regular season championship and were the top seed in the [conference tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Big_East_women's_basketball_tournament "2023 Big East women's basketball tournament"). Azzi Fudd and Caroline Ducharme, who both missed a significant part of the regular season due to injury, returned in time for the Big East tournament, and with the UConn squad healthy for the first time since its first games, the Huskies methodically notched three consecutive wins to emerge as tournament champions, getting the automatic bid to the [2023 NCAA women's basketball tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_NCAA_Division_I_women's_basketball_tournament "2023 NCAA Division I women's basketball tournament"). In the NCAA tournament, UConn advanced to their 29th consecutive Sweet Sixteen with wins over Vermont and Baylor. However, they lost to Ohio St. in the next round, ending their Final Four streak at 14. The Huskies finished their season with a 31–6 record.
texts.8:
With most of their roster either injured or in-development during the season, the Huskies relied heavily on several players for the first time. Mühl, the team's new point guard, set a UConn single-season record with 284 assists. Edwards was the team's leading scorer and a third team All-American. Lopez Sénéchal and Juhász, who had both transferred from other schools in the previous two years, put up solid numbers, as did Griffin, who had missed the previous season.
UConn was ranked no. 2 in both the 2021 AP and Coaches pre-season polls. After some early struggles, they finished the regular season with a record of 22–5, including 16–1 in the Big East to win the conference regular season championship. UConn then won the [Big East tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Big_East_women's_basketball_tournament "2022 Big East women's basketball tournament"). As a no. 2 seed in the NCAA tournament, they advanced to the championship game, where they lost to South Carolina. UConn finished their campaign with a record of 30–6.
The Huskies graduated senior starters Christyn Williams, Olivia Nelson-Ododa, and Evina Westbrook from the 2021–22 roster, each of them being drafted into the [Women's National Basketball Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women's_National_Basketball_Association "Women's National Basketball Association"). Sophomore Piath Gabriel chose to enter the transfer portal during the offseason and accepted a scholarship at UMass.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UConn_Huskies_women's_basketball_team#cite_note-07072022UMassGabrieltransfer-5)

texts.10:
UConn lost two players to knee injuries during the 2022 offseason. On August 1, superstar guard Paige Bueckerstore her left ACL during a pick-up game, and UConn announced two days later that she would miss the entire 2022–23 season.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UConn_Huskies_women's_basketball_team#cite_note-7) Then, during a Huskies practice on October 21, freshman forward Ice Brady dislocated her right patellar tendon; she underwent season-ending surgery on October 25.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UConn_Huskies_women's_basketball_team#cite_note-8)
The Huskies had another excellent recruiting class. ESPN ranked Patterson as the fourth-best recruit of the 2022 class and Brady as the fifth-best. Brady would be lost for the 2022–23 season to a knee injury. Bettencourt was recruited just before the start of the season.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UConn_Huskies_women's_basketball_team#cite_note-9)
